chapter: Hampton, New York and Lee's own band
title: The four-part sound: Gerald Wilson, Dudley Brooks and Strayhorn arrange
summary: The band of trumpet, two tenors and guitar attracted arrangers Gerald Wilson, Dudley Brooks and Billy Strayhorn, and got a Cafe Society offer, but never recorded.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Well, then, they made him do this for 6 weeks, while he put his transfer in, and after that, then he could play with us. We had a very good band, because -- I'll tell you who made the arrangements for us -- Gerald Wilson was making arrangements for us, Dudley Brooks, and Billy Strayhorn.

Yeah, Strayhorn was here, and the reason he was making arrangments for us was because Duke Ellington was in town with the show, "Jump for Joy" -- the "Jump for Joy" was downtown at the Mann Theatre. Was that in '41?

Okay. So the band that we had was quite unique because they had not started using guitars playing parts, so we had 4 part harmony, and this was why Gerald and Dudley and Billy Strayon wanted to write for us, because we had -- which is a big sound; he used a trumpet, 2 tenors and guitar. And you voice that properly, and you have a big sound -- and we did have a big sound.
As a matter of fact, we made so much noise out here, they heard about it back east, and they brought -- Barney Josephson brought us back there to work Cafe Society.
Oh, did you ever record with this group?
Never did. Well, it was a band; it was something, and just a terrible time, because it seems when we really were in to it, there was a band on recording, it seems to me, during that time.
